title: NP membership of context unification
formal: Is satisfiability of finite systems of context equations in NP, with uncompressed input terms, an input finite ranked signature, ordinary variables, and arbitrarily repeated one-hole context variables?
definitions:
A finite ranked signature assigns a nonnegative arity to each function symbol and contains at least one constant. It is explicitly supplied with arities in unary. Ground terms are finite ordered trees whose nodes have the number of children given by their labels’ arities. A ground context is such a tree with exactly one leaf replaced by a hole; the context consisting solely of the hole is allowed. Applying a context C to a term t replaces that unique hole by t.

An input expression may use ordinary variables as leaves and context variables as unary function symbols, in addition to the ranked signature. A solution assigns each ordinary variable a finite ground term and each context variable a finite ground context over that signature. The same assignment is used at every occurrence. After substitution, both sides of every input equation must be syntactically identical trees; equality is not modulo any algebraic identities. Repetitions and nesting of context variables are unrestricted. The input writes all expression trees explicitly, without DAG or grammar compression. Its size includes the signature, identifiers and all written occurrences.

NP membership means one polynomial p and deterministic polynomial-time verifier such that every solvable instance of size n has an accepted binary certificate of length at most p(n), while no unsolvable instance does. Certificates may encode compressed witnesses or other evidence; the actual expanded substitution trees need not be polynomial size. The verifier cannot use an uncharged equality or satisfiability oracle.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked polynomial verifier with soundness, completeness and polynomial certificate length for all unrestricted instances, or prove the decision language is not in NP. An NP result for a bounded number of context variables or a nesting restriction is insufficient. Conditional non-membership must state its complexity assumption.
context:
Jeż establishes a PSPACE upper bound for context unification over finite signatures. This settles decidability but does not supply polynomial certificates.

The paper distinguishes restricted fragments with stronger known bounds. Those fragments are not substituted for the unrestricted equations here.
why: This asks for short certificates at the central remaining complexity boundary for context unification.

import_provenance.original_title: Is general context unification in NP?
import_provenance.original_statement: Can solvability of finite equations between trees containing ordinary variables and one-hole context variables be certified in polynomial size and verified in polynomial time? This is an editorial extension of Niehren and coauthors’ NP result for well-nested context unification to unrestricted instances.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Decidability itself was settled by Jeż; the remaining question is the sharper complexity bound.

sentences: Context variables stand for finite trees with exactly one hole.
A solution consistently substitutes trees and contexts to make all equations identical.
The input allows arbitrary repetitions and nesting.
A polynomial-space algorithm is known, while the target asks for polynomially verifiable certificates.
Compressed certificates are permitted even when expanded substitutions are large.
